summary: One model served from this machine over an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (llama-swap, llama.cpp server, vLLM on localhost). Selecting it as the session's model puts the session on the local lane: every sub-agent dispatch and every compaction runs on that one model, and nothing falls back to a remote provider.

requires.name: a local OpenAI-compatible server
requires.description: A server on this machine answering POST /v1/chat/completions for the model you name. The lane has no remote fallback, so if it is down the session fails loudly instead of switching provider.
requires.howTo: llama-swap: `llama-swap --config <config.yaml> --listen 127.0.0.1:8888`, then check `curl -s http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1/models`. A plain llama.cpp server or vLLM works the same way.

requires.name: {{apiKeyEnv}}
requires.description: The bearer token the backend expects. models.json stores only the $NAME reference, never the value. A server that checks no key still needs the variable set to any non-empty value.
requires.howTo: The installer writes it to ~/.pi/secrets.env (chmod 600, outside the tracked tree) or the macOS Keychain, the same as every other provider key.

prompts.label: Base URL of the local server, including the /v1 suffix
prompts.help: PI appends /chat/completions to what you give here. Use a loopback address: this class means the prompt never leaves the machine.

validate.message: must be an absolute http(s) URL

prompts.label: Name of the environment variable that will hold the backend's API key
prompts.help: The NAME, not the key. You are asked for the value later.

validate.message: an environment variable name in capitals, e.g. LOCAL_API_KEY

prompts.label: Model id, exactly as the server serves it
prompts.help: Get the real list with: curl -s <baseUrl>/models. The lane runs on this one model.

prompts.label: Context window of the loaded model, in tokens
prompts.help: The window the server really allows, not the model card's maximum. On the lane compaction triggers at 75% of this number, so an overstated window means the session overflows before it compacts.

notes: THE LOCAL LANE. When the session's active model belongs to this provider, the harness treats the whole session as local: every sub-agent dispatch runs on the session's model (tier names and explicit provider/model pins are both rewritten to it, and each rewrite is reported), compaction runs on it and never on a remote route, and the remote-fallback hop after an empty reply is not taken. Off the lane nothing changes. This is a deliberate exception to the rule that a dispatch never silently substitutes a model, decided 2026-10-27; see docs/adr/0009-local-provider-lane.md.
NO FAILOVER, EVER. If the local server is down, the turn aborts with the provider, model, error class, message and cause chain. There is no retry on another provider.

THE FOUR ZEROS ARE WRITTEN ON PURPOSE. A local model has no per-token price, so the cost is four literal zeros authored in this fragment, not zeros the installer filled in because nobody asked. The status line reads a flat 0.000 for this provider and that is correct.

THE ALL-NULL thinkingLevelMap AND supportsReasoningEffort false SAY ONLY THAT NO REASONING LEVEL IS STEERABLE HERE. A local server that forces thinking on still returns it as reasoning_content, which PI shows; the harness just never sends reasoning_effort.
CONCURRENCY IS 1. One local model on one machine serves one request at a time; a larger number only queues behind the model swap. Sub-agents on the lane therefore run one after another.
SMALL LOCAL MODELS CALL TOOLS UNEVENLY. The lane works, but a weak model may fail to emit a dispatch or edit call at all; that shows up as a plain model failure, not as a harness fault.

verify.label: the server is up and serves your model id
PI sees the provider as configured
PI can complete one turn through it
